description: Coal seams: peat mires preserved where accommodation kept pace with peat production, after land plants; rank from burial heating.

source.note: peat-mire facies from the strata log (Bohacs & Suter 1997)

driver.note: accommodation roughly matching peat production; excess drowns mires (Bohacs & Suter 1997); numbers are design

notes: No USGS grade–tonnage model exists for coal. Density 1.32 t/m³ for bituminous coal: USGS Circular 891 (Wood et al. 1983), Table 2 p. 22 (1,800 short tons per acre-foot; anthracite 1.47, subbituminous 1.30, lignite 1.29 in data/usgs/coal.json).

PLACEHOLDER tonnage 4.2 / 13 / 25 Mt: one mine-sized block of 1.2 km radius (Circular 891's indicated-reliability radius) × seams of 28, 84 and 168 in (Circular 891 thickness class limits) × 1.32 t/m³ — not a USGS distribution. The aspect follows (a 2 m seam over a 1–1.5 km block).
PLACEHOLDERS: density_per_1e5km2 10 / 30 / 80 (no USGS density), min_separation_m 2400 (two block radii), formation_depth_m 800.

Rank from Lopatin TTI of the coal layer: TTI 75 ↔ Ro ≈ 1.1 % (Waples' correspondence as tabulated by the Kansas Geological Survey, non-USGS; the high-volatile bituminous limit). The lignite, subbituminous and low-volatile bounds are PLACEHOLDERS (no USGS table of reflectance by rank was found).
Design values: the curves, clustering, dip, size_mult_v 20 (a 2 m seam is a tenth of a block at 20 m per block).
